items.definition: You say all when you mean every one, or the whole amount. If you eat all the peas, none are left.
items.definition_previous: every one or the whole amount

definition_basis.note: WordNet has no entry for this word; written by Claude

items.definition: An apple is a round fruit with red, yellow, or green skin. It is crunchy to bite, and you find apples in a fruit bowl.
items.picture_idea: a shiny red apple with a leaf
items.definition_previous: a round red or green fruit that grows on a tree

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: fruit with red or yellow or green skin and sweet to tart crisp whitish flesh

items.definition: A baby is a very small child who cannot walk or talk yet. A baby sleeps and cries a lot.
items.picture_idea: a smiling baby in a diaper
items.definition_previous: a very young child

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a very young child (birth to 1 year) who has not yet begun to walk or talk

items.definition: A ball is a round toy. You can throw it, kick it, or roll it when you play.
items.example: Can you roll the ball to me?
items.picture_idea: a bright red ball on grass
items.definition_previous: a round toy that you throw, kick, or roll

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a spherical object used as a plaything

items.definition: A banana is a long yellow fruit. You pull off the peel and eat the soft, sweet inside.
items.example: She peeled the banana and took a bite.
items.picture_idea: a yellow banana, partly peeled
items.definition_previous: a long yellow fruit with a soft inside and a peel

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: elongated crescent-shaped yellow fruit with soft sweet flesh

items.definition: A bath is when you sit in a tub of water and wash your body.
items.example: It is time for your bath.
items.picture_idea: a child in a tub with soap bubbles and a rubber duck
items.definition_previous: washing your body in a tub of water

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a soaking and washing in a bathtub

items.definition: A bed is a soft thing to lie on at night when you sleep. You lie in it under a blanket.
items.example: I am tired and want to go to bed.
items.picture_idea: a small bed with a pillow and blanket
items.definition_previous: a soft place where you sleep

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a piece of furniture that provides a place to sleep

items.definition: You say big when something takes up a lot of space. An elephant is big, but a mouse is small.
items.picture_idea: a large elephant next to a small mouse
items.definition_previous: large in size

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: above average in size or number or quantity or magnitude or extent

items.definition: A bird is an animal with feathers and wings. Many birds fly, and you see them in trees or the sky.
items.example: The bird is singing in the tree.
items.picture_idea: a small bird perched on a branch
items.definition_previous: an animal with feathers and wings that can usually fly

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: warm-blooded egg-laying vertebrates characterized by feathers and forelimbs modified as wings

items.definition: A book has many pages joined inside a cover. You open it to read the words or look at pictures.
items.picture_idea: an open picture book
items.definition_previous: pages with words or pictures that you read

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: physical objects consisting of a number of pages bound together

items.definition: Say bye when you leave, or when someone else is leaving. You can wave your hand at the same time.
items.picture_idea: a child waving a hand
items.definition_previous: a word you say when you leave

definition_basis.note: WordNet has no entry for this word; written by Claude

items.definition: A car is a machine with four wheels that drives on roads. People ride in it to get places.
items.example: We go to school in the car.
items.picture_idea: a small family car on a road
items.definition_previous: a vehicle with four wheels that people ride in

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a motor vehicle with four wheels; usually propelled by an internal combustion engine

items.definition: A cat is a furry animal with whiskers and a tail. Many people keep one at home, and it says meow.
items.picture_idea: a sitting tabby cat
items.definition_previous: a small furry pet that says meow

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: feline mammal usually having thick soft fur and no ability to roar

items.definition: You say cold when something feels like ice or snow. A cold drink is nice on a hot day.
items.picture_idea: a child shivering in a scarf next to a snowman
items.definition_previous: having a low temperature; not warm

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: having a low or inadequate temperature or feeling a sensation of coldness or having been made cold by e.g. ice or refrigeration

items.definition: You use come to ask someone to move closer to you, or when you move toward a place. Come here!
items.picture_idea: a person waving someone closer
items.definition_previous: to move toward the speaker or a place

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: move toward, travel toward something or somebody or approach something or somebody

items.definition: A cookie is a small, flat, sweet food made in an oven. You can eat one with milk.
items.picture_idea: a round chocolate chip cookie
items.definition_previous: a small, flat, sweet baked treat

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: any of various small flat sweet cakes

items.definition: A cup is a small, open container with a handle. You hold it to drink tea, milk, or water.
items.example: My cup is full of water.
items.picture_idea: a small cup with a handle
items.definition_previous: a small container you drink from

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a small open container usually used for drinking; usually has a handle

items.definition: A dad is a man who has a child. A child says Dad when talking to him.
items.picture_idea: a smiling man holding a child's hand
items.definition_previous: your father

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: an informal term for a father; probably derived from baby talk

items.definition: A dog is a furry animal that barks. Many people keep a dog at home and walk it outside.
items.picture_idea: a friendly dog wagging its tail
items.definition_previous: a furry pet that barks

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a member of the genus Canis (probably descended from the common wolf) that has been domesticated by man since prehistoric times; occurs in many breeds

items.definition: You use down to say something moves to a lower place. When you sit down, you move onto a seat.
items.picture_idea: a child sitting down on a chair, with an arrow pointing down
items.definition_previous: toward a lower place

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: spatially or metaphorically from a higher to a lower level or position

items.definition: You say drink when you swallow water, milk, or other liquid. You can drink from a cup or a bottle.
items.explanation: Drink can also be a noun, meaning something you drink.
items.example: I drink water when I am thirsty.
items.picture_idea: a child drinking from a cup
items.definition_previous: to swallow a liquid

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: take in liquids

items.definition: You say eat when you chew food and swallow it. You eat an apple, a sandwich, or dinner.
items.picture_idea: a child eating with a spoon
items.definition_previous: to put food in your mouth and swallow it

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: take in solid food

items.definition: An eye is the part of the body you see with. You close your eyes when you sleep.
items.explanation: We usually have two, so you often see the plural, eyes.
items.example: Close your eyes and go to sleep.
items.picture_idea: a close-up of an open eye
items.definition_previous: the part of your face that you see with

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: the organ of sight

items.definition: You say finished when you have no more to do. When you are finished with dinner, you stop eating.
items.explanation: On many AAC boards, "all done" or "finished" tells people you want to stop an activity.
items.example: I am finished with my dinner.
items.picture_idea: an empty plate
items.definition_previous: done; with nothing more to do

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: ended or brought to an end

items.definition: A fish is an animal that lives and swims in water. You can see fish in a tank.
items.explanation: The plural is usually the same word: fish.
items.example: The fish swims in the tank.
items.picture_idea: an orange fish in a bowl
items.definition_previous: an animal that lives and swims in water

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: any of various mostly cold-blooded aquatic vertebrates usually having scales and breathing through gills

items.definition: You use get when you go and pick something up so you have it. You get your coat before going outside.
items.picture_idea: a child picking up shoes from the floor
items.definition_previous: to take or receive something

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: go or come after and bring or take back

items.definition: You use give when you hand something to someone so they have it. You give a friend a toy to hold.
items.picture_idea: one hand giving a toy to another hand
items.definition_previous: to hand something to someone

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: transfer possession of something concrete or abstract to somebody

items.definition: You say go when you move from one place to another. You go to school in the morning.
items.picture_idea: a green traffic light or a child walking away
items.definition_previous: to move from one place to another

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: change location; move, travel, or proceed, also metaphorically

items.definition: You say good when something is nice or done well. A good meal tastes great.
items.picture_idea: a thumbs-up
items.definition_previous: nice or well done; not bad

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: having desirable or positive qualities especially those suitable for a thing specified

items.definition: Your hand is the part at the end of your arm. You use it to hold a cup or to wave.
items.picture_idea: an open hand with five fingers
items.definition_previous: the part at the end of your arm with fingers

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: the (prehensile) extremity of the superior limb

items.definition: You feel happy when something good happens, like a party with friends. You often smile when you are happy.
items.example: I am happy to see you.
items.picture_idea: a smiling face
items.definition_previous: feeling glad and joyful

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: enjoying or showing or marked by joy or pleasure

items.definition: You say help when you need someone to make a job easier. A friend can help you carry a heavy box.
items.explanation: Help is also what you say when you need someone to assist you.
items.picture_idea: one person helping another reach a high shelf
items.definition_previous: to make something easier for someone

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: give help or assistance; be of service

items.definition: Here means the place where you are now. You say it when you point to a spot close to you.
items.picture_idea: a finger pointing to a spot on a table
items.definition_previous: in this place

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: in or at this place; where the speaker or writer is

items.definition: Hi is a friendly word you say when you meet someone. You say hi to a friend at school.
items.picture_idea: a child waving hello
items.definition_previous: a friendly word you say when you meet someone

definition_basis.note: WordNet has no entry for this word; written by Claude

items.definition: You say hot when something has a lot of heat, like soup from the stove or a sunny day.
items.picture_idea: a steaming bowl of soup
items.definition_previous: having a high temperature; very warm

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: used of physical heat; having a high or higher than desirable temperature or giving off heat or feeling or causing a sensation of heat or burning

items.definition: To hug is to hold someone close in your arms. You hug a person to show you care.
items.explanation: Hug can also be a noun: "a big hug."
items.example: I hug my mom every morning.
items.picture_idea: two people hugging
items.definition_previous: to hold someone close with your arms

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: hold (someone) tightly in your arms, usually with fondness

items.definition: You say hurt when a part of your body feels pain. If you fall down, your knee might hurt.
items.explanation: The past tense is the same as the base form: hurt.
items.picture_idea: a child holding a scraped knee
items.definition_previous: to feel pain, or to cause pain

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: be the source of pain

items.definition: You say I when you talk about yourself. If you want a snack, you say, "I want a snack."
items.picture_idea: a child pointing to their own chest
items.definition_previous: the word you use to talk about yourself

definition_basis.note: WordNet has no entry for this word; written by Claude

items.definition: You use in to tell where something is. When a toy is in a box, the box is all around it.
items.example: The toy is in the box.
items.picture_idea: a toy inside an open box
items.definition_previous: inside something

definition_basis.note: WordNet has no entry for this word; written by Claude

items.definition: You use it instead of the name of a thing or animal. If you have a ball, you can say, "I like it."
items.definition_previous: a word for a thing or animal you already mentioned

definition_basis.note: WordNet has no entry for this word; written by Claude

items.definition: Juice is a drink made from the liquid inside fruit. You can squeeze an orange to get juice.
items.picture_idea: a glass of orange juice with a straw
items.definition_previous: a sweet drink made from fruit

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: the liquid part that can be extracted from plant or animal tissue by squeezing or cooking

items.definition: You say like when something is fun or tastes good to you. If pizza tastes good to you, you like it.
items.picture_idea: a child smiling at a slice of pizza
items.definition_previous: to enjoy something or think it is nice

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: find enjoyable or agreeable

items.definition: You use look when you point your eyes at something to see it. You look at a truck driving by.
items.picture_idea: a child pointing at something and looking
items.definition_previous: to use your eyes to see something

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: perceive with attention; direct one's gaze towards; look

items.definition: You love someone when you care about them very much and like being with them.
items.explanation: Love can also be a noun, meaning a strong feeling of caring.
items.picture_idea: a red heart
items.definition_previous: to care about someone very much

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: have a great affection or liking for

items.definition: You say make when you build or put things together to get something new. You can make a tower with blocks.
items.example: Let's make a tower with blocks.
items.picture_idea: a child stacking colorful blocks
items.definition_previous: to build or create something

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: create or manufacture a man-made product

items.definition: You say me when you talk about yourself. If you want a ball, you say, "Throw it to me."
items.picture_idea: a child pointing to themselves
items.definition_previous: the word you use for yourself when you are not the doer, such as after a verb

definition_basis.note: WordNet has no entry for this word; written by Claude

items.definition: Milk is a white drink that comes from cows. You can pour it on your cereal.
items.example: I drink milk with my cereal.
items.picture_idea: a glass of milk next to a milk carton
items.definition_previous: a white drink that comes from cows and is full of nutrients

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a white nutritious liquid secreted by mammals and used as food by human beings

items.definition: Mom is what you call your mother, the parent who cares for you. You say, "Mom, come and see!"
items.explanation: In British English, people often say mum.
items.example: Mom is reading me a story.
items.picture_idea: a smiling woman holding a child
items.definition_previous: your mother

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: informal terms for a mother

items.definition: You say more when you want extra, so you have a bigger amount. When your crackers are gone, you ask for more.
items.explanation: Often one of the first words a child uses to ask for another helping or to continue an activity.
items.picture_idea: an empty bowl next to a full bowl of crackers
items.definition_previous: a bigger amount; extra

definition_basis.note: WordNet has no entry for this word; written by Claude

items.definition: You say my for things that belong to you. If a teddy bear is yours, you say it is my teddy bear.
items.picture_idea: a child hugging a teddy bear
items.definition_previous: belonging to me

definition_basis.note: WordNet has no entry for this word; written by Claude
